title: Anyone has seen La Peau Douce/The Soft Skin (1964) from Truffaut?

commenti.body:
To be really cliched, it was made around the time of *Hitchcock/Truffaut* and is Truffaut's most Hitchcockian film. Chabrol is a good comparison, it does feel like a Claude Chabrol movie. 

I quite liked it and think that it's probably Truffaut's second best film, to be honest. 

It's a good, entertaining, suspenseful, psychologically twisted movie. I'm not sure that I really have anything interesting or insightful to say about it but I liked it.

In the Criterion booklet, Molly Haskell calls it "Hitchcockian in its aura of impending doom, the impossibility of escape" and writes that " for my money, it’s one of the director’s finest films, subtle, powerfully adult, and profoundly personal."

Does that make sense to you?

Yes it does.

I agree with how she describes the movie. 

Honestly, this movie took me by surprise. I'm not sure of what I was expecting but I really didn't expect to like it as much as I did. 

And I especially didn't expect to love Françoise Dorléac's character that much. 

She's so charming as Nicole. I also deeply connected with her (maybe it's because I'm around her age and don't quite know what to expect from life either...) and she really touched me in a way that totally surprised me. 

I saw it a few days ago and I'm still thinking about the film and her character. 

Pierre is also a very interesting character. I found him very selfish. He is also such a coward in a lot of ways. 

(I also really liked the ending event though I know it's controversial)

Still, the whole movie is great and, like any good Chabrol's movies, I will be rewatching it a lot (and remark something new with every additional viewing).

Chabrol is quite underrated.

Have you read *Hitchcock/Truffaut*? If not, I'd recommend it.

I haven't read it but, now, I'm intrigued. I'll check it out. 

And yes! Chabrol is very underrated and overlooked in my opinion. I "discovered him this year (I've seen 18 of his movies) and he is now one of my favorites directors. I think it's because his movies are not easily available in North America in comparison to other French directors from that time (like Truffaut, Demy, Godard or Rohmer, etc.). 

Because she made a lot of movies with him, Stéphane Audran is also (and quite sadly) underrated and overlooked in comparison to other French actresses of that time (like Catherine Deneuve, Anouk Aimée or Delphine Seyrig...).
